claims.text: A 31-year-old woman from Lima, Peru presented after five days of progressive severe epigastric pain with fever 38.5°C, early satiety, nausea and two vomiting episodes. Murphy’s sign, hepatomegaly and epigastric tenderness supported initial cholecystitis/obstruction suspicion. Serial liver-function values, cholestatic interpretation and leukocytosis were reported. Ultrasound showed reactive changes, serial wall/size changes and mild intrahepatic duct dilation; MRCP confirmed acalculous cholecystitis and excluded obstruction. Acute HAV serology established secondary AAC; other viral/autoimmune markers were negative. She denied eating outside home or stagnant-source water.
